newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - January 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - January 14.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Times Of India
GOVERNMENT WARNED OVER RESTRAINING INVESTIGATION AGENCY

The Supereme Court has sought the government's explanation on news reports regarding a move to curtail the Central Bureau of Investigation's (CBI) powers. The CBI is probing various scams involving, among others, politicians and bureaucrats. The court asked the attorney general to reply within two weeks regarding any general directions issued to the CBI which may impinge on the investigating agency's powers.
The Pioneer
TAX CRACKDOWN ON POLITICAL PARTIES IMMINENT

The income tax authorities have sought permission for prosecuting major national political parties for failing to submit certified copies of accounts for 1995/96 (April-March). All the national parties including the Congress, Bharatiya Janata Party, Janata Dal, Communist Party of India (CPI) and CPI (Marxist) are said to have submitted annual income tax returns. But they are unaccompanied by statements from auditors certifying their accounts. As per income tax law, an annual return is incomplete without such certificates. A 1995 apex court order makes it mandatory for political parties to file their annual income tax returns.
The Hindustan Times
TERRORIST THREAT LOOMS LARGE

A conspiracy to create panic in the country before the Republic Day celebrations (January 26) was unearthed in its initial stages by the Delhi police. Two alleged members of the notorious Dawood gang were arrested and explosives alongwith switches, timers and detonators recovered from their possession. Meanwhile, Bombay police has increased security at various commercial and strategically important locations. Senior police officials termed it a precautionary measure.
The Economic Times
NEW CONTROL NORMS FOR FOREIGN EXCHANGE DEALERS

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has revised the internal control guidelines for authorised foreign exchange (forex) dealers and banks after 15 years. Under the revised guidelines, the RBI asked all banks and authorised forex dealers to set up global and counter-party exposure limits on all forex transactions. The banks would also be required to establish internal audit departments to look at statutory and regulatory compliance, data processing control and back-office efficiency reviews. The central bank also asked banks to set an upper limit for losses on forex transactions.
INDUSTRIAL DEVELOPMENT BANK TO BE RESTRUCTURED

Booz Allen & Hamilton's recommendation to restructure the country's largest financial institution, the Industrial Development Bank (IDBI), has been cleared. The restructuring aims to transform IDBI into the country's premier wholesale bank. It involves shifting credit sanctioning authority from individuals to committees, devolution of power to zonal and branch offices and introduction of a relationship management system to focus on business from top Indian corporates.
Financial Express
INTERNAL PANEL RECOMMENDS DILUTING GOVERNMENT STAKE

A General Insurance Corporation (GIC) internal committee has suggested privatisation of the corporation with the government diluting its stake to 40 percent. The committee, one of the six set up by the GIC, also suggested the corporation should simultaneously reduce its holdings in its four subsidiaries to 60 percent. The six committees recommended setting up of an independent company for reinsurance, floating GIC Holdings for entry into new areas like banking and cutting hierarchy in the four GIC subsidiaries. The committees have jointly produced the report to prepare GIC for an era when its monopoly in the insurance industry might not remain.
NON-BANKING FINANCE FIRMS TO CREATE RESERVE FUND

All non-banking financial companies (NBFCs) would be required to create a reserve fund by transferring at least 20 percent of their net profit to it every year. The new guidelines also stipulate conditions under which an NBFC can start or carry on business. These include obtaining a certificate from the Reserve bank (RBI) and having a net-owned fund of five million rupees. The RBI was also empowered to determine the policy and issue directions to prevent the NBFC being managed in a manner detrimental to the interests of the depositors. The RBI was also given powers to direct special audit of NBFCs.
ORISSA CLEARS IB VALLEY POWER PROJECT

The Orissa state government approved the guarantee for the controversial AES-Ib Valley power project. The state cabinet, while referring the project to the federal government, suggested further concessions the latter could seek from AES were incentives on plant load factor performance, auxiliary power consumption and plant heat rate. Sources said the cabinet felt there was scope for a further reduction in the tariff rate.
Business Standard
CABINET TO DISCUSS LEVY SUGAR PRICE RISE

A cabinet meeting is scheduled to discuss the levy sugar pricing structure and the redrafted Telecom Regulatory Authority bill. The meeting is being held at a time when the government is discussing a revised cabinet note on the petro-goods price hike issue. A meeting of the cabinet committee on economic affairs is also scheduled.
RUSH FOR CONVERSION OF INDIA BONDS

Nearly 75 percent of the $2.2 billion India Development Bonds (IDBs) may be converted into rupees and foreign currency deposits when they come up for redemption. The high rate of conversion indicates IDBs were purchased by Indians who had transferred funds overseas. Redemption of IDBs in dollars would have meant a huge foreign exchange outflow affecting the reserves and consequently the exchange rate of the rupee. Though with falling exports and increasing oil bill, the rupee was set to depreciate, an arrest in outflow through conversions is expected to ease the pressure. IDBs were issued in the form of promissory notes in January 1992 to non-resident Indians and overseas corporates.
MINIMUM PUBLIC OFFER MAY BE RAISED TO 40 PCT

The government is considering the option of raising the mandatory minimum public offering by companies from 25 percent to 40 percent to jump start the primary markets, sources said. This might form part of the package of measures promised by Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda to pep up capital market sentiment by bringing back the retail investors to the bourses. Sources said the government was, however, unlikely to restore the minimum public offer to 60 percent of a primary issue, which was the practice until 1992 when it was scaled down to 25 percent by the Securities and Exchange Board of India.
MULTINATIONALS IRKED AT INDUSTRY CHAMBER'S STAND

Multinational firms (MNCs) in the Associated Chambers of Commerce and Industry (Assocham) are against the body's stand on foreign investments. An Assocham committee report has sought to limit foreign equity participation in the consumer goods sector at 40 percent. The report is aimed at providing Indian companies with a level playing field to compete with foreign companies. The chamber advocated a cap on foreign investments in the consumer goods sector while allowing MNCs to hold wholly-owned subsidiaries in the infrastructure segment For MNC members, the stand was unacceptable as it was a reversal of the view taken by Assocham in the past.
SWISS PARENT TO PICK UP ABB-ABL PREFERENFIAL SHARES

Asea Brown Boveri (ABB) of Switzerland is picking up seven million preferential shares worth 700 million rupees in ABB-ABL. The boiler manufacturing firm was taken over by ABB India two years ago under a rehabilitation plan. ABB India, which has a 76 percent stake in ABB-ABL, will utilise the amount to revive the company. ABB's application has not been cleared yet as the Industry Ministry is viewing the deal as an external commercial borrowing and not as a direct foreign investment. The deal has been cleared by the central bank.
The Observer
PETROLEUM GOODS PRICE HIKE RULED OUT

Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda has ruled out any move to increase prices of petroleum products. Denying media reports that he had hinted at a rise in prices of petroleum products, Gowda said the press had misunderstood his statement. He said he spoke of the growing deficit in the oil pool account, which stood at around 125 billion rupees. Referring to the last price hike in petroleum products by his government, he said owners of cars and scooters could afford to absorb the rise in prices. The government had imposed a 25 percent price hike on petrol and 15 percent on diesel in July last year, triggering protests from even its coalition partners, particularly left-wing parties.
RANBAXY-CROSSLANDS SWAP RATIO PUT AT 3:7

The swap ratio for the merger between the Delhi-based Ranbaxy Laboratories and Bombay-based Croslands Research Laboratories Ltd has been put at 3:7. Based on the current market price of the two scrips, this swap ratio would give Croslands' shareholders an advantage. The valuation of the two companies was done independently by the respective company auditors. Croslands director V. Shankar said the merger would be effective from April 1, 1996.
DEEMED EXPORT STATUS LIKELY FOR POWER, PETRO KIT MAKERS

The Finance Ministry will accord deemed export status to power and petroleum sector equipment manufacturers. The deemed export status would entitle them to certain duty reimbursement by the government, which they have to pay when their products come out of factories. The equipment manufacturers had been raising this demand through apex chambers for some time. The demand was not accepted as it would incur a 30 billion rupee revenue loss. It was also felt that equipment manufacturers would misuse the facility by importing raw materials on lower duty and selling them in the open market.
